sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: The movement was predicated on **Satyagraha** (truth-force) and **Ahimsa** (non-violence) as political weapons to challenge the moral legitimacy of British rule.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: The **Dandi March** (March 12 – April 6, 1930) served as the symbolic ignition point, transforming the abstract demand for Purna Swaraj into a tangible, mass-participatory issue: **Salt**.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: The movement utilized **Constructive Programs** (Khadi, anti-liquor, anti-untouchability) to build a parallel social base alongside the political agitation.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The movement saw unprecedented participation from women, students, and the business community, marking a significant expansion of the social base compared to the Non-Cooperation Movement.

items.definition: Also known as 'Red Shirts', led by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan in the NWFP; they were non-violent Pashtun activists.
A political truce where Congress agreed to suspend CDM and participate in the Second Round Table Conference in exchange for the release of political prisoners and the right to make salt.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Key Application 1**: Boycott of foreign cloth and liquor shops to hit British economic interests.
• **Key Application 2**: No-tax campaigns in provinces like Bihar and Bengal to paralyze the colonial administrative machinery.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Communal divide, lack of Muslim participation in some regions, and the eventual exhaustion of the mass base by 1934.
• **Solutions**: Shift toward parliamentary politics (Congress Socialist Party formation) and continued focus on rural upliftment.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'D-S-P-C' (Dandi, Salt, Peshawar, Congress-Irwin).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Dandi March starts -> Salt Law broken -> Peshawar/Sholapur uprisings -> Congress-Irwin Pact.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Civil Disobedience Movement' with the 'Non-Cooperation Movement'. Remember: CDM involved the *deliberate violation* of laws, whereas NCM focused on *non-cooperation* with institutions.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Political Socialization' to describe how CDM brought the masses into the political fold, creating a permanent shift in Indian political consciousness.

keyTakeaways: CDM marked the transition from elite-led politics to mass-based political mobilization.
The movement demonstrated the economic vulnerability of the British Raj through boycotts and tax refusal.
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was a tactical pause, not a defeat, allowing the Congress to regroup for future struggles.
